title: Sample preparation protocol for Mass Spectrometry Analysis
author: Manon Gilson

steps.title: Extract Proteins
steps.instruction: Extract proteins from cells using guanidine hydrochloride and ultrasonication.

substeps.instruction: If necessary, wash cells with 1 mL of PBS 1X
Centrifuge samples at 10,000 rpm for 10 minutes and discard the supernatant
Add 50 µL of guanidine hydrochloride to small pellets and 100 µL to larger pellets
Perform ultrasonication (pulse 1, amplitude 20%) for three cycles of 10 seconds each, placing samples on ice between each cycle
Centrifuge samples at 10,000 rpm for 10 minutes
Collect supernatants and store at -20°C

steps.title: Determine Protein Dosage
steps.instruction: Measure protein concentration using a Bradford assay in a 96 well plate.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a standard curve with different dilutions of BgG in triplicates
Dilute samples if necessary
Add 2 µL of samples and 23 µL of water to each well, in triplicates
Add 225 µL of diluted Bradford reagent to each well
Measure the absorbance at 595 nm
Plot OD values and standard protein concentrations to determine sample protein concentration (multiplying by the dilution factor)
Collect 50 µg of proteins and adjust the volume with guanidine hydrochloride to reach the volume of the least concentrated sample
Add 1 µL of Dithioerythritol for every 20 µL of sample
Vortex briefly and incubate for 20 minutes at 56°C and 450 rpm
Add 1 µL of Iodoacetamide for every 21 µL of sample
Vortex briefly and incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature, in the dark
Dilute samples 2X with MS water
Add 4 times the sample volume of cold acetone to each sample
Incubate for a minimum of 1 hour at -20°C (overnight recommended)
Centrifuge at 13,000 rpm for 20 minutes at 4°C
Discard the supernatant and let the residual acetone evaporate for a maximum of 10 minutes

steps.title: Perform Trypsinolysis
steps.instruction: Digest proteins using trypsin and prepare for injection.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a trypsin solution of 0.05 µg/µL with NH4HCO3 buffer (50mM)
Add 20 µL (1 µg) of trypsin to digest 50 µg of proteins, avoiding bubbles
Incubate overnight at 37°C at 450 rpm
Stop trypsinolysis with 5 µL of a 0.5% formic acid solution
Store samples at -80°C for long-term or -20°C for short-term storage
Before injection, centrifuge samples at 13,000 rpm for 20 minutes to pellet remaining residues
